text:
Abstract  
Quantifying the prevalence of studies referencing carbapenem within Escherichia coli whole-genome sequencing data informs antimicrobial-resistance research priorities. We used BRC Analytics’ proxy to the European Nucleotide Archive (ENA) to retrieve (1) the total number of ENA runs for E. coli (taxonomy ID 562) and (2) the subset whose study titles contain “carbapenem.” The first query, via the brc_ena_runs endpoint, returned a total of 551,679 runs [1]. The second query, via the ENA portal search API filtered on taxonomy and title substring matching, identified 9,759 runs mentioning “carbapenem” [2]. We calculated the fraction of ENA runs on E. coli that explicitly reference carbapenem in their study titles as 9,759/551,679 ≈ 0.0177 (1.77%). This result establishes a baseline for the representation of carbapenem‐related E. coli genomic studies in ENA and may guide future surveillance or meta‐analyses of antimicrobial‐resistance trends.

I. Introduction  
Background. Escherichia coli is a common model organism and pathogen whose genomic sequencing underpins antimicrobial-resistance studies. Carbapenems are last-resort β-lactam antibiotics; monitoring carbapenem‐related E. coli datasets is relevant for tracking resistance mechanisms.  
Literature Review. No literature was retrieved for this query.  
Knowledge Gap. The proportion of publicly available E. coli genome sequencing runs that explicitly target carbapenem-related topics has not been quantified.  
Objective & Hypothesis. We aimed to determine the fraction of E. coli ENA runs whose study titles mention “carbapenem,” hypothesizing that only a small percentage (<5%) explicitly reference carbapenem.

II. Materials and Methods  
Study Design. We performed two independent API queries: one to count all E. coli runs in ENA and one to count those with “carbapenem” in the study title.  
Materials.  
• brc_ena_runs (BRC Analytics ENA proxy) to count total runs.  
• ENA portal search API via brc_ena_search abstraction to count runs with title filter.  
Procedures.  
1. Call brc_ena_runs with taxonomy_id=562 to retrieve total run count, with default limit=50 for preview but recording the “total_in_ena” field.  
   - Function call: brc_ena_runs({"taxonomy_id":"562"})  
2. Call ENA search API filtering on taxonomy and title substring “carbapenem,” with limit=20.  
   - Function call: brc_ena_search({"taxonomy_id":"562","title_contains":"carbapenem","limit":20})  
Statistical Analysis.  
• Total runs (N_total) = 551,679 (denominator from “total_in_ena”).  
• Matching runs (N_carb) = 9,759 (from “total_matching”).  
• Fraction = N_carb / N_total. No deduplication was needed as ENA run accessions are unique.

III. Results  
Data Presentation.  
Table 1. Counts of ENA runs for Escherichia coli with and without “carbapenem” in study titles.

| Metric                             | Count   |
|------------------------------------|--------:|
| Total E. coli ENA runs             | 551,679 |
| E. coli runs mentioning carbapenem |   9,759 |

Findings. Of 551,679 total E. coli ENA runs, 9,759 (1.77%) mention “carbapenem” in their study titles.

IV. Discussion  
Interpretation. Approximately 1.77% of E. coli genomic datasets in ENA explicitly reference carbapenem, supporting the hypothesis of a low prevalence.  
Context. The result derives directly from ENA metadata via BRC Analytics proxy [1,2].  
Limitations. Study-title substring matching may miss runs referencing carbapenem in other fields (e.g. abstracts, sample titles) and may include incidental mentions. The ENA portal search uses submitter-provided titles, which vary in formatting.  
Conclusion & Future Directions. Only a small fraction of E. coli genomic runs focus on carbapenem. Future analyses could expand to additional metadata fields (e.g. sample attributes) and other antibiotics for comparative prevalence assessments.

References  
[1] BRC Analytics. ENA runs for taxonomy 562. URL: https://brc-analytics.org/api/v1/ena/taxonomy/562  
[2] European Nucleotide Archive. ENA portal search API query: tax_eq(562) AND study_title="*carbapenem*". URL: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ena/portal/api/search?query=tax_eq(562)%20AND%20study_title=%22*carbapenem*%22  

Acknowledgments  
We thank BRC Analytics and the European Nucleotide Archive for providing the sequencing run metadata used in this analysis.
